newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steady to off before tender results.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steady to off before tender results.

text.p: NWE naphtha ended steady to lower on Tuesday after crude stabilised at weaker levels and traders detected continued buying in the swaps.
Traders also awaited results of the Egyptian tender for 1997, which some expected as soon as Wednesday or Thursday.
Rumours circulated that it may be awarded at a premium between $6 and $6.50 over mean fob Med prices.
One source said the result, based on a cif basis, could mean that the tender is above the 1996 tender of mean fob plus $9 because of a change in the methodology used by Platt's.
Traders detected some incremental petrochemical demand for the high paraffinic material that was supporting the NWE physical market.
A trader at a Belgian refinery was having difficulty selling a 5,000 tonne barge of full range naphtha in Northwest Europe for delivery from November 15 at high quotes plus $1.
But he said tighter supplies of higher paraffinic may force users to look for full range grades.
Nov swaps slipped about $1.50 to $221.50 and December fell 50 cents to $215, pulling back from unchanged levels after crude's early drop, traders said.
